correctness.rationale: The smooth conic XZ−Y² and the three triangle secants intersect transversely at the three distinct triangle vertices. For the four parameters t=±1±√2 the distinct extra lines are t²X−2tY+Z=0; restricting one to [1:s:s²] gives (s−t)². Pairing roots of t²−2a t−1 with a=±1 gives the quartic in the finding. Two tangents with distinct parameters s,t meet at [1:(s+t)/2:st], off the conic; this point lies on a secant precisely when s+t=0, s+t=2, or 2st=s+t respectively. These tests give the four listed off-conic triples and no other tangent pair plus secant incidences. No three tangents concur because the corresponding equation in t would be a nonzero quadratic with three roots. No tangent contains a triangle vertex. All 21 line pairs and all 14 conic–line multiplicity units are accounted for, yielding six transverse double points, four simple tangencies, and seven ordinary triples. Their local forms A1, A3 and D4 contribute 1, 3, and 4 respectively, hence τ=46. Independent arithmetic in integer pairs representing Q(√2) confirmed the incidence signatures; sparse Jacobian coefficient columns yielded rank 45/45 modulo 101 in degree four and rank 59/63 over Q in degree five, without relying on the frozen selected minor. These ranks give mdr=5 over C, since ranks over Q and C agree and any lower-degree syzygy could be multiplied to degree four. The sharp du Plessis–Wall expression at (9,5) is 64−15−3=46.
residual_risks: The ranks certify characteristic zero; no uniform claim in positive characteristic
Sharpness is at fixed mdr=5, not a global Tjurina maximum for every degree-nine curve
